options.metric: Annual total pedestrians killed (sum of number_of_pedestrians_killed)
options.denominator: All crash records in each calendar year; the metric is a sum, not a rate
options.reason: A bar chart makes the requested discrete year-by-year totals easy to compare.
options.interpretation: This framing answers the requested year-by-year count; the annual totals are highest in 2013 (176) and lowest in 2020 (101). It is defensible because it sums the pedestrian-killed field across all crash records for each requested calendar year, and bars make discrete annual values straightforward to compare. It does not answer how pedestrian fatality risk changed relative to population, walking volume, or vehicle travel, because those exposure denominators are absent. It excludes rows outside the requested years—2012: 100,545 rows (4.43% of all file rows); 2026: 36,424 rows (1.61% of all file rows); it excludes no 2013–2025 rows for NULL crash dates or pedestrian-fatality counts, and no included year is partial.
